description: Expected stage-4 (take_segmenter) output when fed the canonical transcript. Three takes, each annotated with its quality breakdown. The `overall_score` value is a transparent weighted sum of the sub-scores using default weights — see backend/services/take_segmenter.py once implemented. The values here are the *target* the segmenter must produce within 0.05 tolerance.

takes.text: Hello and welcome back to my channel. Today I want to, uh, talk about something really cool.
takes.clean_text: Hello and welcome back to my channel. Today I want to talk about something really cool.

takes.text: Today I want to talk about something interesting, uh, something that I think you'll find fascinating.
takes.clean_text: Today I want to talk about something interesting, something that I think you'll find fascinating.

takes.text: Welcome back to the channel. Today I want to discuss a fascinating topic that I think you'll really enjoy.
takes.clean_text: Welcome back to the channel. Today I want to discuss a fascinating topic that I think you'll really enjoy.

notes: Take 2 has lower wpm than take 1 because of the longer trailing word ('fascinating') stretching the duration.
Take 3 wpm is intentionally low (long final 'enjoy' tail at 4 seconds) — this is a real artifact of speakers letting the last word ring. Segmenter must not penalize a long final word as a 'pause'.
Quality scores assume default weights. If weights change, all three expected_overall_score values must be updated together — they are not independent.
